skill.name: microsoft-graph-api
skill.description: Use Microsoft Graph API scripts to read Outlook email, send messages, and manage Microsoft 365 calendar events.
skill.summary: Access Outlook mail and Microsoft 365 calendars through authenticated Microsoft Graph scripts.
skill.author: BLTGV

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and reconnaissance hits are false positives caused by TypeScript template literals, documentation code fences, and command examples. The real risks are authenticated access to Microsoft Graph, the ability to send mail or create events, and local OAuth token storage in a JSON file. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: OAuth tokens are stored in a local JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Store tokens with restrictive file permissions, document the risk, and prefer platform secret storage where available.

remediation.issue: Email and calendar write actions can run from command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sending email or creating events, and show the intended action before execution.

remediation.issue: Graph endpoints are assembled from user-supplied values.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers, search text, dates, and recipient addresses before building Microsoft Graph requests.

best_practices: Confirm recipient, subject, and body with the user before sending email.
Use separate profiles for work and personal accounts.
Ask for the smallest required data range when reading messages or events.
anti_patterns: Do not send email or create events without explicit user approval.
Do not request broad mailbox data when a specific search is enough.
Do not store shared or service account tokens in a user profile.

faq.question: What Microsoft services does this skill access?
faq.answer: It accesses Outlook mail and Microsoft 365 calendar data through Microsoft Graph.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Microsoft device code authentication and stores the resulting token locally.

faq.question: Can it send email?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send email when the signed-in account grants the Mail.Send permission.

faq.question: Can it create calendar events?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create events when the signed-in account grants calendar write permissions.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: The scripts store OAuth credentials in a JSON file under the user configuration directory.

faq.question: Does it handle large result sets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It limits results with top values and does not implement full pagination.
